speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in view of the recent incidents of flooding and forecast of inclement weather due to the Indian Ocean Dipole over the next two months, what are the Ministry’s plans to mitigate against flooding, especially in areas where there are major roadworks.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether she can provide an update on the flood management measures and early warning system in view of the recent flooding.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Ministry has conducted a comprehensive review of areas that are susceptible to flash flood situations like what was experienced on the morning of Friday, 20 August 2021; and (b) what plans are being made to mitigate such possibilities from recurring going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Recently, we saw widespread flooding caused by a record rainfall in parts of Europe, China and the USA.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore has also experienced intense rainfall events in recent months.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On 17 April and 24 August, more than an entire month’s rainfall fell on our western parts within three to four hours.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Given climate change, we must prepare for more extreme weather scenarios as we are likely to see more flash floods from intense rain.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Minister, are you taking Question Nos 43 to 45 together?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will continue to monitor these flood-prone areas closely.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is, however, not practical to expand all 8,000-plus kilometres of our drains and flood protection infrastructure to accommodate every extreme rainfall event, as this would require massive land take and much higher costs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Flash floods arising from intense rainfall occur in limited areas and are transient – most will subside within 30 minutes, given our extensive drainage system.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Moreover, PUB deploys more immediate and practical measures to protect our properties against flash floods, including portable flood barriers that can be installed at doorways or erected on roads and pavements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These flood barriers protect residents and businesses against flash floods and minimise potential damage to their premises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB is using technology to better predict and respond to floods.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will help forecast locations which will face heavy rainfall, issue earlier public alerts and enable early deployment of portable flood barriers in areas at risk of flash floods.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Coupled with an extensive network of water level sensors and CCTVs installed at flood-prone areas, PUB’s Quick Response Team can also be deployed on site faster and assist premises owners to set up flood barriers, if needed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Information on floods and road closures is communicated to the public promptly through radio broadcasts, news media, myENV Mobile App, PUB Facebook and Twitter, as well as LTA’s Expressway Monitoring Advisory System.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SMS alerts are also sent to those who have registered to receive flood warnings.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These measures will also help build preparedness to extreme weather events and strengthen community resilience, as we check weather advisories and warnings and adjust our daily schedules accordingly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I encourage members of the public to subscribe to NEA’s and PUB’s SMS alerts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will continue to strengthen our forecasting and sensing capabilities and implement cost-effective measures to minimise flood risks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: However, PUB cannot minimise flood risks on its own.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Building owners must ensure that flood prevention measures in their developments remain effective.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Contractors must also implement proper flood prevention measures at their worksites.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have seen cases of contractors failing to do so, resulting in floods in their locations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This brings me to the flash flood incident that occurred on 20 August 2021.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This flash flood was reported at the junction of Tampines Avenue 10 and Pasir Ris Drive 12 towards TPE entrance at around 8.00 am.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB’s Quick Response Team was immediately deployed to assist drivers and pedestrians, together with SCDF and Police.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB also issued advisories to motorists and members of the public to avoid the area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This location is not a flood-prone area and the drainage system is more than adequate to cope with the rainfall intensity experienced on 20 August 2021.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB’s investigations found that the contractor carrying out road widening works along Tampines Avenue 10 had altered the public drainage system there without PUB’s approval.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As a result, storm water could not discharge effectively into downstream Sungei Api Api.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Under the Sewerage and Drainage Act, no one can carry out any works to alter our storm water drainage system without PUB’s approval.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB also requires contractors working in the vicinity of any watercourse to put in place measures to prevent construction materials from falling and choking up the drainage system.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB takes a serious view of all works that affect our public drainage system.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have reminded all contractors to comply with the requirements and will take enforcement action against errant contractors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We know that we have an increasing number of roadworks, infrastructure works for the next few years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Do we need to toughen up our laws so that contractors know that they will be in serious trouble if they do not comply with the regulations?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second one is: how are we coordinating from an inter-agency perspective so that all agencies, if they are part of the roadworks, can coordinate so that we have less of such occurrences like the one in Tampines in future?

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: The Clerk will proceed to read the Orders of the day.
